messages:
lucy: heads-up — we're seeing intermittent request stalls for model rwi-compact on runtime 3.2.9 in ap-south starting ~04:05 UTC. p95 is drifting and a small subset of requests time out after 8s. not a hard outage but customer impact on streaming.
marco: saw that on the dashboard. traces show a thread interrupt during scheduling when seq > 1500 and batching > 6. looks like an interrupt/scheduler collision.
june: runtime 3.3 rolled earlier this week, but ap-south got a partial 3.2.9->3.3 canary swap yesterday. could be regression in the new scheduler. prefer a regional mitigation vs global rollback.
deploybot: Deploybot: Compatibility advisory detected for model=rwi-compact runtime=3.3. Suggested mitigations: 1) regional pin rwi-compact to runtime 3.2.9 for ap-south, 2) apply safelist routing for low-qps customers, 3) create rollback lane. Commands: `/deploy pin --model rwi-compact --runtime 3.2.9 --region ap-south --duration 24h --reason "scheduler-interrupt-stalls"`
lucy: i'd like a targeted pin + a reduced-batch routing for heavy longseq customers to avoid hitting the scheduler path while we triage. also capture additional traces with full stack and sampling 5%.
marco: agree. will add a routing rule to divert requests with tokens >1200 to a reduced-batch pool and increase trace sampling for that cohort.
qa-bot: QA-bot: queued focused regression job rq-77012 to simulate longseq + concurrent batching. ETA 16m.
marco: executing pin now:
```
/deploy pin --model rwi-compact --runtime 3.2.9 --region ap-south --duration 24h --reason "scheduler-interrupt-stalls"
```
returning task id 142700.
deploybot: Deploybot: Pin executed (task 142700). Safelist routing applied: customers with <4qps routed to runtime 3.2.9. Reduced-batch routing enabled for token-length >1200. Rollback lane rb-142700 created.
sre-oncall: monitor set: abort and re-route if timeouts >= baseline * 1.5 for 10m. also raising alert to paging if errors > 2x baseline.
june: infra: can you try a small scheduler tweak on a canary subset to reduce interrupt preemption? if that helps we can unpin sooner.
infrastructure: canary patch scheduled on a small pool in ap-south within 30m; will report results.
marco: initial telemetry after pin: pinned cohort p95 improved from 520ms -> 280ms, timeouts down 78% for routed customers. overall region improves ~7%.
qa-bot: regression complete for rq-77012: simulated longseq across 1200-2500 tokens; observed reduced stall frequency in reduced-batch routing, divergence <0.4% on outputs. uploading logs to ticket INF-7091.
lucy: good. propose phased-unpin plan if patch validates: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 15m holds and auto re-pin if p95 > baseline * 1.25. record in runbook.
june: created phased-unpin job id pu-142700 and added guardrail: `monitor.policy.add("rwi-compact-ap-south", metric="p95", window=10m, threshold=1.25, action="re-pin")`. also added a note to release-notes: "ap-south: temporary regional pin for rwi-compact to runtime 3.2.9 while investigating scheduler interrupt stalls on 3.3."
sre-oncall: will keep an eye on traces. if canary scheduler tweak shows improvement we can unpin after a short soak (2h). otherwise maintain pin and escalate to eng-runtime for a full revert.
marco: can we also add a short customer-facing blurb in the status page about "intermittent streaming stalls in ap-south for a small subset of customers; mitigations in place" so support gets fewer pings?
lucy: yes please. release coordinator can craft wording.
qa-bot: will run an additional smoke test after canary patch deployed. ETA 45m for full results.
infrastructure: canary patch rolled to pool id canary-51; early traces show reduced preemption events by ~60% for the patched pool.
sre-oncall: promising. keep pin for min 2h while canary soaks. if stable, we'll run the phased-unpin job tomorrow 02:00 UTC. otherwise keep pin and open a rollback PR.
lucy: thanks everyone. keeping this thread as the coordination source; post final unpin schedule or rollback decisions here. :white_check_mark:"
